newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Dow leap lifts Australian stocks at open.
newsitem.headline: Dow leap lifts Australian stocks at open.

text.p: The second largest leap by the Dow lifted the Australian share market at the open on Wednesday, although turnover remained subdued ahead of local March quarter inflation data to be released near the end of morning trade.
The All Ordinaries index jumped 21.7 points to 2,469.3.
The solid underlying tone of recent days remained with the strength in the Dow providing encouragement for local buyers.

The consumer price index (CPI) is due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT) and trade may pick up once that data had been assessed, brokers said. Inflation is set to remain very low, with most forecasting a rise of just 0.1 percent in the headline rate.
"I don't know that people are expecting any surprises from the CPI but you may well get some more interest after that is out of the way," said a Sydney-based broker.
Industrial and resource bluechip stocks were keenly sought.
Elsewhere, West Australian regional Bankwest added two to A$2.54 (US1.98) after posting a full year net profit of A$94.5 million.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of six to one, while about 35 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
